gen-gf-happy-monkey-clash-grotesk: Clash Grotesk keeps its lines smooth and unmodulated. Happy Monkey up top is the loud one, with wide-open e shapes and a ruler-straight stroke, while the body font simply gets on with being friendly.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-fs-hind: Hind has lowercase that nearly matches its capitals, with strokes steady as a drawn string. And Happy Monkey, bold and a bit cheeky above it, leaves the text to run along smoothly without any fuss.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-albert-sans: Loud meets tidy. Happy Monkey carries a ruler-straight stroke and wide-gapped e shapes up top, and Albert Sans keeps its apertures open even at tiny sizes, so the two never compete.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-almarai: Almarai holds a line width that never swells or tapers, and its letters never pinch shut. And Happy Monkey, bold and distinctive above it, gives the text a lively head start.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-anta: Wide gaps in the e give Happy Monkey its cheek. Anta answers with wire-bent letters of constant thickness and gaping mouths, so the loud heading and the approachable text each keep their own character.
